title: Bernstein MGF bound for a centered chi-squared summand
statement: Fix an integer $k \ge 1$, and let $Y$ be a real-valued random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ whose law is the centered Gaussian $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$ of mean $0$ and variance $1/k$. Then the centered square $Y^2 - 1/k$ satisfies the Bernstein MGF condition on $(\Omega, \mu)$ with quadratic-growth parameter $c = 2/k^2$ and radius $t_{\max} = k/4$.
hypotheses_covered: k a natural number with 0 < k
Y is measurable / a genuine random variable
the law of Y is the centered Gaussian N(0, 1/k)
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{centered\_chi\_squared\_step}, the
centered summand $Y^2 - 1/k$ satisfies
$\text{\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}}\bigl(2/k^2,\;k/4\bigr)$ under $\mu$.
